chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Isma'il al-Khorasani, from Al-Ridha (peace be upon him)
He said: Not abandoning something is the restraint (himyah) from it; rather, the restraint from something is doing it less often.

key_terms.إِقْلال: Doing something less often; moderation in frequency or quantity.
key_terms.حِمْيَة: Restraint, moderation, or dietary restriction; avoiding excess.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between abstaining and moderation in Shia Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) refutes the extreme asceticism of the *Wara'* school by defining *himyah* not as total abstinence, but as moderate consumption to prevent excess. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual discipline with the enjoyment of lawful worldly pleasures, ensuring that moderation serves as a safeguard against greed rather than a rigid prohibition. Such nuanced ethical guidance reflects the broader Imami tradition of integrating practical daily life with spiritual refinement.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-67 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Isma’il al-Khorasani that Al-Ridha (s) said, “
Abstaining from something does not imply abandoning it. Rather it implies doing it less often.”
